Name: RT-LIM-01 Switching BurnIn/Calibration radio reloads correct groups in combobox
Objective: Verify that switching between BurnIn and Calibration radio buttons replaces the groups combobox contents with the corresponding group type entries.
Precondition: Application launched. Protocols parsed with both BurnIn and Calibration data present. At least one BurnIn group and one Calibration group exist in their respective YAML files.
Test Script (Step): Switch to the Statistics tab. Select the BurnIn radio button under Show Groups.
Test Script (Expected Result): BurnIn radio is selected. The group name label and combobox reflect BurnIn group entries only.

Test Script (Step): Note the group names visible in the groups combobox.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group names are from BurnInLimGroups.yaml.

Test Script (Step): Click the Calibration radio button.
Test Script (Expected Result): The groups combobox immediately reloads with Calibration group entries only. No BurnIn group names remain visible.

Test Script (Step): Click the BurnIn radio button again.
Test Script (Expected Result): Groups combobox reverts to BurnIn group entries. No crash and no error in the log.

Name: RT-LIM-02 Forward/Back navigation cycles through all groups without skipping
Objective: Verify that pressing Group > and < Group navigates through every available group in sequence and wraps correctly.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated (ST-09). At least three groups are defined in the active group type YAML file.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Select the BurnIn radio. Note the first group shown in the group name label.
Test Script (Expected Result): First group is shown. Stats table rows reflect that group's limits.

Test Script (Step): Click Group > repeatedly until the last group is reached.
Test Script (Expected Result): Each click advances to the next group in order. Stats table updates after each click. No group is skipped.

Test Script (Step): Click Group > once more (past the last group).
Test Script (Expected Result): Navigation wraps to the first group OR the button is disabled/has no effect — no crash.

Test Script (Step): Click < Group from the first group.
Test Script (Expected Result): Navigation wraps to the last group OR the button is disabled — no crash.

Name: RT-LIM-03 Stats table Cg column populated when upper and lower limits are defined
Objective: Verify that the Cg (process capability) column shows a numeric value when a limit row has both Upper Limit and Lower Limit defined, and shows '-' or empty when they are not.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated with a limits YAML that has at least one entry with both upperLimit and lowerLimit defined, and at least one entry with no limits.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Load the standard limits YAML via Load Input Config File.
Test Script (Expected Result): Path label updates.

Test Script (Step): Click Parse/Write Statistic to recalculate.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table repopulates. Rows with both Upper Limit and Lower Limit non-empty show a numeric value in the Cg column. Rows with no limits show '-' or an empty Cg cell.

Name: RT-LIM-04 Error column reflects limit violations correctly
Objective: Verify that the Error column of the stats table is populated with an error indicator for limit rows where the measured value exceeds the configured limits, and is empty/OK for passing rows.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. At least one limit has a value that exceeds its upper or lower boundary in the parsed data.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Click Parse/Write Statistic.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table is populated.

Test Script (Step): Inspect the Error column for the limit row known to exceed its boundary.
Test Script (Expected Result): The Error cell for that row shows a non-empty indicator (e.g. 'ERR', a coloured cell, or a non-zero value). Rows within limits show an empty or 'OK' Error cell.

Name: RT-LIM-05 Extend Input Limits File merges new limits with existing ones
Objective: Verify that enabling 'Extend Input Limits File' on the Burn-In tab appends new limits from the selected file rather than replacing existing ones.
Precondition: Application launched. A base BurnIn limits YAML is already loaded (shown in the path label). A second YAML with additional (non-overlapping) limit entries is available.
Test Script (Step): On the Parse Protocols tab, switch to the Burn-In sub-tab. Check 'Extend Input Limits File'.
Test Script (Expected Result): Checkbox is checked.

Test Script (Step): Click Load Input Limits File and select the secondary YAML.
Test Script (Expected Result): File dialog closes. Path label updates to the secondary file path.

Test Script (Step): Click Parse/Write Statistic on the Statistics tab.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table contains limit rows from both the base YAML and the secondary YAML. No rows from the base file were removed. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-06 Extend Limits Groups File merges group entries from two YAML files
Objective: Verify that enabling 'Extend Limits Groups File' appends group entries from a second YAML to the combobox without removing existing groups.
Precondition: Application launched. BurnIn groups file is loaded. A second groups YAML file with at least one unique group entry is available.
Test Script (Step): On the Parse Protocols tab, switch to Burn-In sub-tab. Check 'Extend Limits Groups File'.
Test Script (Expected Result): Checkbox is checked.

Test Script (Step): Click Load Limits Groups File and select the second groups YAML.
Test Script (Expected Result): Path label updates.

Test Script (Step): Switch to the Statistics tab, select BurnIn radio, and inspect the groups combobox.
Test Script (Expected Result): The combobox contains group entries from both the original and the second YAML file. No group from the original file is missing. No crash.

Name: RT-LIM-07 Save Group dialog shows error label when Group Name is empty on Save
Objective: Verify that clicking Save in the LimitsGroupsSaveDialog with an empty Group Name field displays an inline error and does not close the dialog.
Precondition: ST-16 passes. Save Group dialog is open.
Test Script (Step): Leave the Group Name field empty. Add at least one valid limit entry in the Limits table.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group Name field is blank. Limit cell has a value.

Test Script (Step): Click the Save button.
Test Script (Expected Result): The dialog remains open. The error label displays a non-empty message indicating that the group name is required (e.g. 'Group name cannot be empty'). No group is added to the combobox.

Name: RT-LIM-08 Save Group dialog shows error when all Limit cells are empty on Save
Objective: Verify that clicking Save with at least one row filled in the Group Name but no valid limit entries shows an error and does not close the dialog.
Precondition: ST-16 passes. Save Group dialog is open.
Test Script (Step): Type a valid group name in the Group Name field. Leave all Limit cells in the table empty.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group Name field is filled. All Limit cells are empty.

Test Script (Step): Click Save.
Test Script (Expected Result): Dialog remains open. Error label shows a message indicating at least one limit must be defined. The combobox is not updated.

Name: RT-LIM-09 Multiple series on dual Y-axes render correctly without overlap
Objective: Verify that enabling multiple series with different axes (ax1 and ax2) renders both axes with independent scales, correct labels, and no visual artifact or crash.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. At least two limit rows with Graph = 'On'.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Set row 0 Graph = 'On', Axis = 'ax1'. Set row 1 Graph = 'On', Axis = 'ax2'.
Test Script (Expected Result): Both rows show Graph = 'On'. Row 0: ax1, Row 1: ax2.

Test Script (Step): Inspect the plot frame.
Test Script (Expected Result): Primary (left) Y-axis shows the row-0 series. Secondary (right) Y-axis shows the row-1 series. Both Y-axes have independent scales. No series is missing. No crash.

Test Script (Step): Resize the application window.
Test Script (Expected Result): Plot redraws at the new size. Both axes and series remain visible and correctly scaled.

Name: RT-LIM-10 Clear button on Statistics tab resets table and plot
Objective: Verify that clicking Clear on the Statistics tab empties the stats table and clears the plot frame without affecting parsed protocol data.
Precondition: Statistics tab is populated with rows (ST-09 passed). At least one row has Graph = 'On' so the plot is non-empty.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Confirm stats table has rows and plot frame has series.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table has rows. Plot is non-empty.

Test Script (Step): Click the Clear button on the Statistics tab.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table row count becomes 0. Plot frame clears (no series lines visible). Group name label resets. Group combobox is empty or reset. No crash.

Test Script (Step): Switch to another tab and back to Statistics.
Test Script (Expected Result): Statistics tab still shows empty state. No phantom data reappears. Application does not crash.

Name: RT-LIM-11 Export .pptx with ax2 series includes secondary axis data in slides
Objective: Verify that when one or more series are on ax2, the exported .pptx file contains slides with the secondary axis data and not just the primary axis.
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. Row 0 Graph = 'On', Axis = 'ax1'. Row 1 Graph = 'On', Axis = 'ax2'. output/ is writable.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Set up two series on ax1 and ax2 respectively as above.
Test Script (Expected Result): Both series are plotted in the frame.

Test Script (Step): Click Export .pptx.
Test Script (Expected Result): Export completes. A new .pptx file appears in output/. File size > 0.

Test Script (Step): Open the .pptx file and inspect slides for the ax2 series.
Test Script (Expected Result): At least one slide contains the secondary-axis (ax2) data series. The slide is not blank. No error in the log.

Name: RT-LIM-12 Load Input Config File with invalid JSON shows error in log and does not crash
Objective: Verify that loading a malformed or invalid .json file as the statistics input config logs an error and leaves the tool in a stable state.
Precondition: Application launched. A file named invalid_config.json containing invalid JSON (e.g. missing closing brace) is accessible.
Test Script (Step): Click Load Input Config File.
Test Script (Expected Result): File dialog opens.

Test Script (Step): Select invalid_config.json and click Open.
Test Script (Expected Result): File dialog closes. Path label updates.

Test Script (Step): Click Parse/Write Statistic.
Test Script (Expected Result): An ERROR-level entry appears in the log table describing the parse failure. The stats table remains empty or unchanged. The application does not crash or freeze.

Name: RT-LIM-13 Contains match with no matching limits produces empty filtered group view
Objective: Verify that navigating to a group whose Contains match string has no matching limit names in the stats data results in an empty stats table view (not a crash).
Precondition: Statistics tab populated. A group exists in the combobox that uses Contains match with a substring not present in any parsed limit name.
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Navigate to the group with the non-matching Contains filter using Forward/Back buttons.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group name label shows the group name.

Test Script (Step): Inspect the stats table.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table shows 0 matching rows. The plot frame shows no series. No crash. No ERROR entry in the log.

Name: RT-LIM-14 Duplicate group name in Save Group dialog is rejected or overwrites correctly
Objective: Verify that attempting to save a group with a name that already exists in the combobox either raises a clear error or asks for confirmation before overwriting.
Precondition: ST-09 passed. At least one group named 'ExistingGroup' is present in the active groups combobox.
Test Script (Step): Open the Save Group dialog. Type 'ExistingGroup' in the Group Name field.
Test Script (Expected Result): Group Name field shows 'ExistingGroup'.

Test Script (Step): Add a valid limit entry and click Save.
Test Script (Expected Result): One of the following occurs: (a) an error label indicates the name already exists and the dialog stays open, or (b) a confirmation prompt appears asking whether to overwrite. No silent duplicate is created without user confirmation.

Name: RT-LIM-15 Statistical Series button after Clear does not crash
Objective: Verify that clicking Statistical Series immediately after Clear (when the stats table is empty) does not crash the application.
Precondition: Statistics tab is visible and the Clear button has been clicked (table is empty).
Test Script (Step): Switch to Statistics tab. Click Clear to ensure the table is empty.
Test Script (Expected Result): Stats table row count = 0.

Test Script (Step): Click the Statistical Series button.
Test Script (Expected Result): Application does not crash. Either a 'no data' message is shown in the plot frame or the plot simply shows an empty series. No ERROR-level entry in the log.
